paper.title: Choosing Answers in Epsilon-Best-Answer Identification for Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: (epsilon, delta)-PAC best-answer identification in transductive linear Gaussian bandits
unmapped: transductive: the answer set Z (finite, size Z) differs from the arm set K
epsilon-optimality may be additive or multiplicative
the parameter set M is known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: We consider the transductive linear bandits setting, where the collection of arms K ⊆ R^d and answers Z ⊆ R^d are finite sets ... observes X_t = ⟨µ, a_t⟩ + η_t ... The noise η_t ∼ N(0, σ^2) ... we consider σ^2 = 1. ... we assume that the set of parameters is bounded, i.e. there exists M > 0 such that for all µ ∈ M, ∥µ∥_2 ≤ M.

settings.name_in_paper: (epsilon, delta)-PAC best-answer identification in transductive linear Gaussian bandits (lower bound)
unmapped: transductive: the answer set Z differs from the arm set K
epsilon-optimality may be additive or multiplicative
the parameter set M is known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: A strategy is said to be (ε, δ)-PAC if, for all µ ∈ M, with probability at most δ it terminates while not recommending an ε-optimal answer ... our goal is to minimize the expected sample complexity E_µ[τ_δ].

algorithms.name: GLR stopping rule (5) with threshold (6) and any recommendation z_t in Z_eps(mu_{t-1}) (modified BAI algorithms)

symbols.T_eps: characteristic time T_ε(µ) of ε-BAI, T_ε(µ)^{-1} = max_{z∈Z_ε(µ)} max_{w∈Δ_K} inf_{λ∈¬_ε z} (1/2)||µ−λ||^2_{V_w}

conditions: ||µ||_2 <= M for all µ in M
holds for both additive and multiplicative ε-optimality
tuning: L^K learner with sub-linear regret (e.g. AdaHedge)
Z-oracle returns z̃_t ∈ z_F(µ_{t-1}) (exact furthest answer)
exploration bonus f(t)=2β(t,t^{1/α}) with α=3, b=1

source.quote: Let L^K with sub-linear regret (e.g. AdaHedge) and L^Z returning z̃_t ∈ z_F(µ_{t−1}). Using (6) as stopping threshold β(t, δ), LεBAI yields an (ε, δ)-PAC algorithm and, for all µ ∈ M such that |z_F(µ)| = 1, lim sup_{δ→0} E_µ[τ_δ]/ln(1/δ) ≤ T_ε(µ).

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality; matches the lower bound of Theorem 2.1. The exact Z-oracle is computationally intractable (paper says so), hence compute not_stated. Algorithm is also (ε,δ)-PAC.

symbols.T_g_eps: greedy characteristic time, T_{g,ε}(µ)^{-1} = max_{z∈z*(µ)} max_{w∈Δ_K} inf_{λ∈¬_ε z} (1/2)||µ−λ||^2_{V_w}; strictly larger than T_ε(µ) iff z_F(µ) ∉ z*(µ)

conditions: for all asymptotically greedy (ε, δ)-PAC strategies

source.quote: For all asymptotically greedy (ε, δ)-PAC strategy, for all µ ∈ M, lim inf_{δ→0} E_µ[τ_δ]/ln(1/δ) ≥ T_{g,ε}(µ) where the inverse of the greedy characteristic time is T_{g,ε}(µ)^{-1} = max_{z∈z*(µ)} max_{w∈△K} inf_{λ∈¬ε z} 1/2 ∥µ − λ∥^2_{V_w}, and T_{g,ε}(µ) > T_ε(µ) if and only if z_F(µ) ∉ z*(µ).

results.notes: Asymptotically greedy: strategies that asymptotically only stop on greedy answers z*(µ).

conditions: any sampling rule; recommendation z_t ∈ Z_ε(µ_{t-1}) for all t in an infinite set of times T

source.quote: Let T ⊆ N with |T| = ∞. Given any sampling and recommendation rules such that z_t ∈ Z_ε(µ_{t−1}) for all t ∈ T, then evaluating the stopping criterion (5) at each time t ∈ T with the threshold β(t, δ) = 2K ln(4 + ln(t/K)) + K C_G(ln(1/δ)/K) yields an (ε, δ)-PAC strategy.

results.notes: δ-correctness guarantee of the stopping-recommendation pair, recorded as error probability ≤ δ; does not need the bound M.

cited_results.cited_title: Pure exploration with multiple correct answers
cited_results.setting_description: (ε,δ)-PAC ε-best-answer identification in transductive linear Gaussian bandits (σ^2=1), additive or multiplicative ε-optimality; corollary of the multiple-correct-answers lower bound; for all (ε,δ)-PAC strategies
